C3-05-L01 — Why distributed processing: partitions, executors and coordination

FAILURE TO CATCH
Using Spark for tiny data can add complexity without benefit.
C3-05-L02 — Spark architecture, driver and execution model
MENTAL MODEL
Driver plans/co-ordinates; executors perform tasks over partitions; actions trigger lazy work.
FAILURE TO CATCH
Confusing driver memory with executor/partition work leads to unsafe collect/toPandas usage.
C3-05-L03 — PySpark DataFrames and explicit schemas
MENTAL MODEL
Schema is an input contract: types, nullability and parsing rules should be explicit for production data.
FAILURE TO CATCH
InferSchema can turn malformed values into nulls or inconsistent types without deliberate rejection
logic.
C3-05-L04 — Selecting, filtering and expression design
MENTAL MODEL
Use native column expressions so Spark can optimize; keep transformations declarative and
inspectable.
FAILURE TO CATCH
Python row loops/UDFs can hide logic and block optimizer benefits.
C3-05-L05 — Joins and distributed join consequences
MENTAL MODEL
Before joining, prove grain/key uniqueness and choose strategy from sizes/distribution; joins can
shuffle or multiply rows.
FAILURE TO CATCH
A many-to-many join can be logically wrong even when Spark completes quickly.
C3-05-L06 — Aggregations, grouping and window functions
MENTAL MODEL
Aggregations change grain; windows add context while preserving row grain when designed
deterministically.
FAILURE TO CATCH
Window without deterministic ordering creates unstable rankings/ties.
C3-05-L07 — Nulls, types and data-cleaning patterns
MENTAL MODEL
Separate invalid/rejected rows from clean rows; never silently drop malformed facts.
FAILURE TO CATCH
Casting invalid text to numeric null then filtering nulls loses evidence and breaks reconciliation.
C3-05-L08 — Reading and writing CSV/JSON/Parquet/Delta
MENTAL MODEL
Input/output format, schema and partition strategy are operational contracts; Parquet output needs
file-count reasoning.
FAILURE TO CATCH
Writing one file per task/partition can create tiny-file problems or accidental single-file bottlenecks.
C3-05-L09 — Spark SQL and DataFrame interoperability
MENTAL MODEL
SQL and DataFrame APIs compile into the same optimizer world; choose the clearest expression and
validate result parity.
FAILURE TO CATCH
Switching APIs does not fix wrong grain or bad keys.
C3-05-L10 — Partitions, repartition, coalesce and shuffles
MENTAL MODEL
Partition changes trade parallelism, network shuffle and output file count.

Assert dimension key uniqueness first. A valid many-to-one join should preserve clean fact row count

State output grain and independently reconcile grouped totals to the clean control metric.

Use deterministic partition/order/tie rules and prove window preserves fact-row grain.
PLAN
Formatted explain must identify scans, exchanges/shuffles and join strategy; tuning decisions refer to

Measure key distribution/task behavior. Hot key classification is separate from malformed-row quality
handling.
PERFORMANCE DECISION
Broadcast/repartition/coalesce/cache/AQE choice must have before/after evidence and unchanged
correctness controls.
OUTPUT
Parquet file/partition strategy should match data size and downstream use; avoid coalesce(1) by habit.
TESTS
At least two tests/invariants should catch row loss/duplication, schema or rejection/join errors.
REPEATABILITY
CLI-style job captures Spark/Python/Java versions, parameters, output path/run evidence and rerun
behavior.
Green-but-wrong states to reject
•
Spark job is green but malformed row disappeared with no rejected artifact.
•
Broadcast join is fast but duplicate dimension key multiplied facts.
•
AQE changed the plan but output grain/metric was never reconciled.
•
Hot key is optimized as skew even though it actually represents bad source data.
